fresh_terms.name: ~x
fresh_terms.purpose: client DH exponent generated randomly with 1 < x < q

fresh_terms.name: ~y
fresh_terms.purpose: server DH exponent generated randomly with 0 < y < q

long_term_keys.name: host_ltkS
long_term_keys.policy: private server host signing key; public host key is RFC field K_S; reveal only via explicit Reveal(...) if later modeled

messages.label: M0C
messages.meaning: C's identification string V_C and SSH_MSG_KEXINIT message I_C have been exchanged before the selected DH exchange begins; they are opaque transcript inputs included in H.
messages.protection: none; pre-exchanged context outside the selected section
receiver_must_treat_as_opaque: I_C contents not parsed in this IR

messages.label: M1
messages.meaning: C sends its DH public value e computed from fresh exponent x.

messages.label: M0S
messages.meaning: S's identification string V_S and SSH_MSG_KEXINIT message I_S have been exchanged before the selected DH exchange begins; they are opaque transcript inputs included in H.
messages.protection: none; pre-exchanged context outside the selected section
receiver_must_treat_as_opaque: I_S contents not parsed in this IR

messages.label: M2
messages.meaning: S sends its public host key K_S, its DH public value f = exp(g,~y), and a host-key signature s over exchange hash H_S = HASH(<V_C,V_S,I_C,I_S,K_S_pub,e,f,K_Srv>) where K_Srv = exp(e,~y).
messages.protection: digital signature authenticates H_S under K_S_pub when the client verifies both the host-key binding and the signature; no encryption
receiver_must_treat_as_opaque: signature algorithm internal second hash, if any

checks.condition: Generate random x satisfying 1 < x < q and compute e = exp(g,x) mod p.
Generate random y satisfying 0 < y < q and compute f = exp(g,y) mod p.
After receiving e, compute K_Srv = exp(e,~y) and H_S = HASH(<V_C,V_S,I_C,I_S,K_S_pub,e,f,K_Srv>) with the exact RFC field order.
After receiving K_S_recv, f, and s, compute K_C = exp(f,~x) and H_C = HASH(<V_C,V_S,I_C,I_S,K_S_recv,e,f,K_C>) with the exact RFC field order.
Verify that received K_S_recv really is the host key for S, represented as trusted_host_key(C,S,K_S_recv).
Optional RFC-allowed branch: accept the received host key without verifying trusted_host_key(C,S,K_S_recv); this branch is explicitly insecure against active attacks.
Verify s as a valid signature on H_C under the verified server host key K_S_recv.
Verify s as a valid signature on H_C under the received but untrusted K_S_recv.
For the first key exchange, set session_id = H_C; once computed, the session identifier is not changed by later re-exchanges.
For the first key exchange, set session_id = H_S; once computed, the session identifier is not changed by later re-exchanges.
Use the same HASH algorithm to derive IV, encryption, and integrity keys from K_C, H_C, literal letters A-F, and session_id; extend by repeated HASH(<K,H,key_so_far>) if needed.
Use the same HASH algorithm to derive IV, encryption, and integrity keys from K_Srv, H_S, literal letters A-F, and session_id; extend by repeated HASH(<K,H,key_so_far>) if needed.

compromise.policy: No explicit reveal, corruption, host-key compromise, exponent reveal, or session-key reveal behavior is mentioned in the selected protocol input. Record exact reveal/corruption events, exposed values, and lemma exception timing if later modeling input introduces compromise.

abstractions: RFC binary encodings and concatenation are represented as ordered tuples inside HASH; field order is preserved.
V_C, V_S, I_C, and I_S are modeled as opaque pre-exchanged transcript values because the input excludes the rest of SSH negotiation.
K_S_pub is the RFC public host key field K_S; it is separated from shared secret labels K_C and K_Srv to avoid name collision.
The host-key trust check is represented by a predicate trusted_host_key(C,S,K_S_recv), standing for certificates or a local database.
The RFC-allowed accept-without-verification behavior is preserved as a separate insecure optional client branch.

Key derivation output lengths and taking prefixes of hash output are abstracted by kdf_initial, kdf_extend, and take_prefix; the A-F labels and extension dependency on K, H, and accumulated key material are preserved.
Later re-exchanges are not modeled as full protocol runs; only the constraint that the first H becomes session_id and remains unchanged is recorded.
No validation of received DH public values e or f beyond the computations described in the selected text is added.
modeling_assumptions: Use the standard Dolev-Yao adversarial network model.
Model only the protocol behavior described by the current IR and modeling contract.
Do not use the reference Sapic+ or Tamarin models during generation; they are evaluation metadata only.
The selected input is limited to RFC 4253 Section 8 key exchange and Section 7.2 key derivation; application data protection and user authentication are out of scope.
Public parameters p, g, q and role names C and S are available to both parties and the adversary.
The goals are user-supplied metadata; expected satisfying results are preserved but do not remove the RFC-stated unverified host-key acceptance branch.

semantic_constraints.policy: M1 precedes M2: C sends e before S computes K_Srv, H_S, and s.
S computes f = exp(g,~y), K_Srv = exp(e,~y), H_S = HASH(<V_C,V_S,I_C,I_S,K_S_pub,e,f,K_Srv>), and s = sign(H_S,host_ltkS).
C computes K_C = exp(f,~x), H_C = HASH(<V_C,V_S,I_C,I_S,K_S_recv,e,f,K_C>), and verifies s against H_C under K_S_recv.
If M1 and M2 are both honest and K_S_recv = K_S_pub, then K_C = K_Srv by the DH equation.
The exchange hash H includes V_C, V_S, I_C, I_S, K_S, e, f, and K in exactly that order.
Client host authentication requires both trusted_host_key(C,S,K_S_recv) and successful signature verification on H_C.
The unverified client branch omits trusted_host_key(C,S,K_S_recv) by design and is explicitly marked insecure against active attacks.
The first exchange hash H is the session identifier; once computed it remains unchanged across later re-exchanges, which are otherwise not modeled.
The same HASH algorithm used in key exchange must be used in key derivation.

Initial IV/key formulas are HASH(<K,H,'A',session_id>) through HASH(<K,H,'F',session_id>) for client-to-server IV, server-to-client IV, client-to-server encryption key, server-to-client encryption key, client-to-server integrity key, and server-to-client integrity key respectively.
If more key bytes are needed, derive K1 = HASH(<K,H,X,session_id>), K2 = HASH(<K,H,K1>), K3 = HASH(<K,H,K1,K2>), and so on, taking the needed prefix.
The selected section provides explicit server authentication, not an explicit client-authentication mechanism.
